content:
After the release of the seventh developer beta of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and Apple's other upcoming software updates, Apple is now rolling out the corresponding public beta versions. Here are the details.

Apple releases new public beta versions

Apple released this morning:

  • iOS 27 developer beta 7 (build 24A5424a)
  • iPadOS 27 developer beta 7 (build 24A5424a)
  • macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 7 (build 26A5421a)
  • tvOS 27 developer beta 7 (build 24J5358a)
  • visionOS 27 developer beta 7 (build 24M5359a)
  • watchOS 27 developer beta 7 (build 24R5358a)

Apple is now rolling out the corresponding versions to public beta testers — this is the fifth round of public beta releases. So far, Apple has released new public beta versions for iOS 27, tvOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and HomePod 27.

Today's releases don't include any particularly notable changes, as Apple is now mainly focused on bug fixes and stability improvements in preparation for the official launch expected in a few weeks.

In addition, Apple has also released the second public RC version of macOS Sequoia 15.8 (24H20), following the release of the corresponding developer RC version earlier this morning. The second RC version of macOS Tahoe 26.7 (25G224) is expected to be released soon. These are also available starting at 7:42 PM Eastern Time.

Among all of today's releases, the public beta versions have the exact same build numbers as the developer versions.

Enroll in the Apple Public Beta Program

If you would like to enroll your devices in the public beta program, please visit https://beta.apple.com and follow the steps for each corresponding device. Here's how to install a public beta version on your iPhone:

  • Visit the Apple Beta Software Program website and choose to enroll or sign in.
  • Sign in with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone, then accept the program terms and enroll your account.
  • Open Settings on your iPhone.
  • Go to General > Software Update > Beta Updates.
  • Select iOS 27 Public Beta.
  • Return to the Software Update screen, and when the beta version appears, tap Update Now.

Apple recommends installing beta software on a secondary device. If you're using your primary iPhone, make sure to back it up beforehand.

Have you spotted any changes in today's beta versions? Let us know in the comments.
